detailed_description:
Photoreal cinematic live-action, 1881 London, 35 mm film grain, natural weight and pace.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:05. The shot begins from <Picture 3>: a medium shot from behind <Subject 1>'s bottle-green velvet shoulder at his own table under the tall arched window, the same laboratory seen from its middle: he is turned to the table, dark wavy hair; a long bodkin raised in the hand on the left of frame; the hand on the right of frame, his right, with the small plaster on its forefinger, over the litre vessel of clear water; the blue flame beside the vessel. The camera holds a static shot as <Subject 1> pricks the fingertip with the bodkin and sets the bodkin down on the bench in the first 2 seconds, from 00:00 to 00:02. At 00:02 he squeezes the finger and lowers the hand to the mouth of the vessel. At 00:03 a drop falls into the water and the hand draws back and reaches for a pipette on the bench, and the reach continues to the last frame of the shot. Behind him one student in shirtsleeves at a far bench under the window, his back turned, writing, from 00:00 to 00:05. <Subject 1>'s mouth is closed from 00:00 to 00:05 while he pricks the fingertip with the bodkin.
[Shot 2] From 00:05 to 00:09. At 00:05 the shot cuts to an extreme close-up at the same place on the bench, beginning from <Picture 4>: the plastered forefinger above the litre vessel, a single drop of blood hanging from the fingertip, the water below perfectly clear, the blue flame reflected in the glass. The camera is at the mouth of the litre vessel itself, a hand's breadth from the glass and level with its rim, a macro lens. The camera holds a static shot as the drop falls from the fingertip into the water and a red thread sinks through the clear water to the bottom of the vessel, from 00:05 to 00:07. At 00:07 the plastered finger lifts out of the top of frame and a glass pipette comes down into the vessel from above, and the lift continues to the last frame of the shot. Behind him one shirtsleeved shoulder at the far bench, fallen to a soft dark ground beyond the glass, from 00:05 to 00:09.
[Shot 3] From 00:09 to 00:16. At 00:09 the shot cuts to an extreme close-up of the vessel on the bench, beginning from <Picture 5>: the one thin red thread hanging in nearly clear water, the flame in the glass; the bench and the glass alone in frame, the vessel's rim the only edge above the water. The camera is set down on the bench top a hand's breadth back from the vessel. The camera holds a static shot as the pipette tip releases drops into the water and lifts out of the top of frame, from 00:09 to 00:11. At 00:11 the water darkens from the red thread outward to dull mahogany, a brownish dust settling to the bottom. At 00:14 <Subject 1>'s plastered hand comes in from the right, picks the vessel up and tilts it toward the camera by the cut, and the movement continues to the last frame of the shot. Behind him one student in shirtsleeves at a far bench beyond the glass, his back turned, fallen soft, from 00:09 to 00:16.
